notes.title: August Update – Quests, Rivals, Evenings and Art!
notes.content:
[h3][b]Hey Guildmasters![/b] [/h3][p]August has been a busy month both on the dev and commissioned art side![/p][h3]🎮 [b]Development update: Quests, Rivals & Evenings![/b][/h3][list][*][p]The [b]Evening Phase[/b] is now "functional" but right now more "ctionnal " than "fun"😅 
(but don't worry I know exactly what i want to try for it to become challenging and fun). I had to rework injury and gear degradation system and do a first pass at balancing those to prepare work on this. [/p][/*][*][p]The [b]Recruitment Draft[/b] was refined once again: rivals now behave more “humanly” (they don’t cheat with hidden info any more ), bidding ties can be resolved with new (world fitting) mechanics, and I added a first pass at a tutorial to help players through their first draft.[/p][/*][*][p]The [b]Quest system[/b] has been reworked to allow for more truly different quests. The system can now handle: escalating threats, repeatable tasks tied to resources, and unique quests with custom rules! This will also ensure a richer narrative for the game![/p][/*][/list][h3]
🎨 [b]Illustrations Incoming![/b][/h3][p]Big news: I’ve officially started working with illustrator [b]Clockwork Tony[/b] ([url="https://clockworktony.bsky.social"]bsky[/url] | [url="https://x.com/clockwork_tony"]Twitter/X[/url])![/p][p]She will be bringing [b]incident reports[/b], [b]POI discovery and day phase transitions[/b] to life.
These illustrations will add flavor and immersion every time something happens in the guild. Here’s a first finished (the first we worked on and others are even better but I want to keep some secret for later or even you to discover in the game) 

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45322556/a7959111c4f65c557803469e562b78dbd8a1d87f.png"][/img][/p][p]🎶 [b]Music Progress[/b][/p][p]The main theme is also in the works! We’ve settled on the main melody and production has begun. It’s going to really shape the atmosphere of the game and I'm eagerly awaiting it![/p][hr][/hr][p][i]Vincent L.
[/i]

notes.title: Jully Update – Dev progress and more illustrations for the game!
notes.content:
[h3][b]Hey Guildmasters![/b] [/h3][p][i]note: This news was written 14 days ago but stayed in draft...[/i]😆[i]
[/i][/p][h3][b]🎮 A mix of balancing the Draft, implementing the Evening phase and refining Quest generation.[/b][/h3][p]While fine-tuning the Recruitment Draft proved a real balancing act (I would say it is 85% done) work moved on to the next phase needing refinement: the [b]Evening Phase[/b].  This phase is all about services to the adventurer and back office work. That's the moment when you choose what will be served at the tavern, the price of "bone mending" and also move all those toggle and knobs to be sure everything runs smoothly. It’s almost functional, and a rough interactive UI helps me test it before refining further.[/p][p]Other dev and design work this month:[/p][olist][*][p][b]Refined request/quest generation[/b] to better reflect faction alignments[/p][/*][*][p]New [b]onboarding tools[/b]: nested tooltips, highlights, and more[/p][/*][*][p]Continued to work on adventurer's [b]sprite variations[/b] and animation.[/p][/*][*][p]Cleaned some old code[/p][/*][*][p]Wrote more of [b]the lore and world "logic "[/b] especially around [b]factions[/b] and their power struggles[b].[/b][/p][/*][/olist][h3]
🎨[b] Signed with an illustrator![/b][/h3][p]After reviewing [b]150+ illustrator submissions[/b] (😅), I’ve selected the artist who’ll bring the game’s [b]incident reports[/b] (previously called "events") to life! They’ll work on 30+ illustrations to help each story beat and random event feel even more unique and immersive. Can’t wait to share some of the results soon.[/p][hr][/hr][p][i]Even though I currently don't have anything visual to share, I’m really happy with dev progress and the feel of the game, I'm having a blast making it and I hope you will have a blast playing it once it is out!   See you next month at the latest[/i][/p][p][i]Vincent L.
[/i]

notes.title: May Update - Things are starting to come together!
notes.content:
[b]Hey Guildmasters![/b]

May has been all about connecting the dots. I've been away to recharge post-Kickstarter and it turns out the fresh air and coding outside was what I needed! The game is finally shaping up into a cohesive experience and the "Adventurers Guild Inc." I envisioned seems closer to reality than ever!

A lot of previously isolated pieces are now working together and progress has been good on both the Ui and code. I’ve been able to lock in key decisions, am finally entering the proper production phase, and it feels awesome!

[h3][b]🛠️ Development Update: [/b][/h3]
Over the past few weeks, I’ve:
- Assembled the full structure of the in-game week, with placeholder and early versions of each phase. I've also hooked up the already working core simulation with the Ui prototypes.
- Refined key game systems, including the recruitment loop, event forecast, and daily reports
- Begun overhauling the visual feedback and UI so everything feels more responsive, readable, and intuitive

The trickiest design challenge has been balancing player guidance vs. player agency, especially when it comes to evaluating candidates and assigning them to roles. I want you to be able to make an informed choice not an obvious/mandatory one or a blind pick.

[h3][b] 👀 Sneak Peek: Visuals in Progress[/b][/h3]

Still WIP but happy with the result and learned a lot from it.

- Full code review (to clean and future-proof core systems, some refactoring should happen this month)

- Reorganising the Discord (adding private backer channels and onboarding new members)
- Preparing for commissions including music, translation and new custom art.

So not much to show visually but a neat "production pipeline" that should speed everything up in the weeks and months ahead.

notes.title: Feature Deep Dive No. 1 : Adventurers
notes.content:
[h1]👋 Greetings, Guild Masters![/h1]
Today, we’ll take a look at one of the core components of the game: [b]Adventurers[/b]: who they are, what they do, and how you can help them succeed!
[h2]1. What are Adventurers?🔮[/h2] 
[list]
[*] [b]"Adventuring" is a job![/b] Like carpentry or soldiering, its main goal is to provide an income for those doing it, ideally without them dying in the process.
[*] It’s a [b]well-compensated, regulated job[/b]. The pay matches the risk, but the right to wield weapons, throw fireballs, and venture into the unknown means someone has to keep an eye on them (that’s you!).
[*] You[b] provide them with quests, support them[/b] in various ways (see below), and[b] nudge them in the right direction[/b]. If they succeed, you will too!
[*] They are not your employees nor simple customers and even if you [b]don’t control them directly[/b] they are at the center of your operation. That’s why your staff, facilities, and management tools will be crucial in keeping everything running smoothly.
[*] And finally, adventuring is in demand! Even if you start with a dozen applicants, expect this number to steadily grow to reach [b]several hundred[/b].
[/list]🎮In-game: Indirect control of hundreds of adventurers through most other systems.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45322556/67917cc3301d8362464c930bb15243313f411ca6.png[/img]
[i]Can you guess who these adventurers are ?[/i]

[h2]2. Get to Know Them! 🔍[/h2]
No two adventurers are the same! To unleash their full potential, you will have to get to know them better than they know themselves (literally).
[list]
[*] It’s up to you to call them by their [b]names[/b] or by their ID, but even if you don’t need to recognize each one of them, getting a sense of who is a mage and who can wield a sword by looking at their [b]outfit[/b] could come in handy!
[*] Don’t worry, your staff will get their[b] background, affiliation[/b], and, after some tests, might even be able to determine their [b]potential[/b] or their exact [b]attributes & skills[/b]!
[*] A well-kept secret is that the [b]Adventurer ID[/b] is embedded with a tracking and appraising spell. While they have it on them, you can track where they go, what they do, how much they have, if their stamina is low, and so on!
[/list]🎮In-game: Basic data on adventurers is always available but to dig deeper and get a full picture, effort and resources will be needed!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45322556/a17cd6af2c91db040a2aa2a6aa84cf46ee05a45d.gif[/img]
[i]Current version of the adventurers' needs updating dynamically in the ledger[/i]

[h2]3. Help Them Grow 📈[/h2]
A good Guildmaster knows that first impressions aren’t everything! Some of your best adventurers might start as complete nobodies while others may fail to live up to expectations.
[list]
[*] [b]Everyone starts with some stats![/b] Whether it's from a past job or some training on the side, you don't really care, as long as they put these to use ASAP. 
[*] Quests, training, haggling, even having a chat at the tavern are occasions to [b]grow along the path you choose for them.[/b]
[*] But should adventurers focus on their [b]current strengths[/b] or on what they could become based on their [b]potentials[/b]?
[*][b]Training[/b] could even help them learn new skills and the worst of the bunch could, in time, exceed their potentials!
[*] [b]Adventurers’ ranks[/b] are a big deal! Higher-ranked adventurers will have [b]different needs[/b] but will face [b]higher challenges[/b]. Promotion tests are required but you could also use your [b]Guild Master authority[/b] to jumpstart a protégé!
[*] [b]Injuries, death[/b], or a[b] lack of questing[/b] opportunities might lead an adventurer to become “definitely unavailable”. There are some things that even a reviving spell can’t solve!
[/list]🎮 In-game: Adventurer attributes grow based on their potential and their assigned role. Training can influence potential and skills. Rank promotion is distinct from levels and is a whole event in itself.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45322556/7520268e3e0679933a23dff684c89e6ce5d7d950.png[/img]
[i]The attributes on an adventurer card (this Ui is a bit outdated and is being reworked to include an emphasis on potential for each stats instead of a global value) [/i]

[h2]4. What Do Adventurers Actually Do? ⚔️[/h2]
Adventurers aren’t just waiting around for orders; they have their own routines, needs, and ambitions.
[list]
[*] Adventurers arrive in the morning and then [b]decide what to do:[/b] go on quests, train, stay at the Guild, or return home.
[*] Before and after quests (or while staying at the guild), adventurers will automatically[b] try to meet their needs[/b] (rest, healing, gear, entertainment, etc.). An injured adventurer will seek healing services, but if your infirmary is overcrowded or the prices are too steep, they will look elsewhere!
[*]They [b]decide what is best for them[/b] based on their [b]adventuring attribute[/b] and how much to spend based on [b]business traits[/b]. It’s up to you to decide whether you should keep them in the dark or help them make more informed choices.
[/list]🎮In-game: Adventurers are independent. Most will choose a path that mitigates risk while ensuring enough earnings to buy gear, heal, and set some money aside. But some will look for riskier options or spend all their money at the tavern instead of upgrading their gear. That’s where you (and your staff) come in!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45322556/208da4cd2660aa2361db6b575067499db485112a.gif[/img]
[i]A test on using animated sprites as feedback on what adventurers are doing (here training) sprites and animations from LyanSek [/i]

[h2]5. Deeper Dive: Adventurer Quest Choice🎯[/h2]
[list]
As we’ve seen, Adventurers make calculated decisions. They don’t just randomly pick quests or activities. 
[*]Each quest and training session has an appeal score, based on your guild’s facilities, marketing, and events.
[*] Adventurers evaluate all available options and assign an Affinity Score by combining their preferences (e.g., hates mountains), adventuring stat (matching quest requirements), and the quest reward (while deducting travel and gear costs).
[*] The highest-affinity adventurer picks first, but quest slots are limited, so adventurers may have to go with their secondary choices.
[*] At some point, if they can’t pick many of their choices or if the affinity score for remaining quests is too low, they simply won’t pick any.
[/list]🎮In-game: The appeal system lets you control what is globally interesting, while the affinity system makes each adventurer decide based on their own goals and needs.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45322556/97a328974973aec0ce68fc61cfa446edcd3ca876.png[/img]
[i]An illustration of the process. In game with up to 300 adventurers choosing from 50+ quests that  would be too chaotic to display like this! Currently, adventurer sprites simply move to their chosen quest without showing their thought process, but I’m working on improving that![/i]

[h2]6. How to Shape Adventurers Then? 📋[/h2]
Adventurers might act on their own, but you have plenty of tools to shape their journey.
[list]
[*] The first step is to choose wisely who can become adventurers. Through the[b] recruitment process,[/b] you can exclude certain backgrounds or traits, choose who to dismiss, and [b]assign roles[/b] to those you admit based on their recruitment tests.
[*] Ensuring (through clever [b]promotions[/b])  that adventurers’ ranks match their capacities is the simplest way to make sure an adventurer takes the right quests and doesn’t buy stuff they don’t need.
[*] Adventurers tend to follow your staff’s advice, and[b] you can use “tags”[/b] in the ledger to [b]nudge them in the “right” direction[/b] (after all, perhaps you do want them to buy stuff they don’t need! 😉).
[*] Meeting their needs and [b]investing in better facilities[/b] is a good way to make sure they grow to their full potential, but with limited funds and staff, you will have to [b]choose what path to take[/b].
[*] Finally, you can turn your hard-earned[b] prestige[/b] into [b]Guild Master authority[/b] to send them on mandatory quests, promote them, or fire them, but beware of the potential consequences.
[/list]
[i]Current WIP of the recruitment system... [/i]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45322556/692985ef4662d07cf7551db775069f82a5f33794.png[/img] 
[i]...and here is the WIP of the tag system![/i]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45322556/304133971a1f955b5f098900a441a5866e8b63e8.png[/img]
[b]
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------[/b]

[h1]What's Next? 📆[/h1]
✅ All adventurer mechanics are fully implemented.
✅ Quests, training, and decision-making work as intended.
✅ The Adventurer Ledger updates dynamically to reflect status changes.

[b]Current focus No. 1: [/b][b]Improving feedback on decisions[/b], including reports, logs, and more visual cues like thought bubbles or animated UI elements.
[b]Current focus No. 2: [/b][b]Making the guild feel more immersive[/b] by refining visual sequences with more varied adventurer sprites and animations.
[b]
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------[/b]
[b]💬 That’s it for this deep dive! Have questions? Drop them in the comments or join the [url=https://discord.gg/eYkh76H8WT]Discord[/url]!

✨ Wishlist the game on Steam & stay tuned for an upcoming epic announcement coming this month![/b]
[b]
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------[/b]
https://store.steampowered.com/app/3297040/Adventurers_Guild_Inc/

notes.title: January Dev Update: 2025 Roadmap
notes.content:
[h2]Greetings, Guildmasters! 👋[/h2]
First and foremost, I wish you [b]all the best for 2025![/b] May it be filled with awesome games, old and new! As for Adventurers Guild Inc., the journey continues, and it’s time to take a look at where we are and where we’re heading this year. 

[b][h3]A Look Back at 2024:[/h3][/b][list][*][b]Q1 2024:[/b] Start of the project.
   [*][b]Q3 2024:[/b] First working prototype of the core simulation. I began sharing the journey on social media.
   [*][b]Q4 2024:[/b][list]
     [*]Steam Page Launch and Bluesky Growth: Over 2,000 followers joined the guild!
     [*]Turn-based management gameplay with a day/night cycle.
     [*]Fully implemented quest production chain (exploration, negotiation, transformation, and publishing) + balancing of 375 quest variants (30 of which are currently fully fleshed out with visuals and descriptions).
     [*]Stress test of the independent adventurer simulation, with 300 adventurers taking quests (using the affinity system) and managing their needs.
    [*]And more, such as the tech tree, starting biases, and the first version of the facilities management menu.[/list][/list][b][h3]First feedback on what’s currently in the game:[/h3][/b]At the end of 2024, I put parts of the game into testers’ hands for the very first time. Here’s what I learned:
[list]
[*]     The guild and adventurer simulation feels “complex and deep,” which was my primary goal! So this was a relief! 
[*]     The tone and feel of the game was a pleasant surprise for many testers. One comment I loved was that many elements felt “like a board game.”
[*]     The biggest missing piece they noted was the lack of visual representation for adventurers, the guild, and animations in general, which I 100% agree with.[/list][b][h3]Looking Ahead: The Roadmap[/h3][/b]Here’s what I can confidently promise for 2025: better visuals, more content, and a playable version for testers to enjoy.
My main areas of focus will be:
[list][*]Visual Sequences: Once you end the current turn, watch the guild come to life. Key areas include quest tracking on the world map, adventurer recruitment, and guild activity sequences.
[*]Replacing Temporary Visuals: Many placeholders used in early development will be replaced, and sound will be added to enhance feedback and immersion.
[*]Content Creation: Continuing to write content that fits the game’s “chaotic humor” tone.
[*]First Playtest or Demo: Planned for Q3 2025 at the earliest.[/list][b]
[h3]When will the game release ? In what state ?[/h3][/b]While I aim to release Adventurers Guild Inc. by the end of 2025, I won’t rush to meet this deadline. 
I will organize playtests and perhaps release a demo during the course of 2025, but I won’t release the game in Early Access. If something is essential for the core game experience to work, it will be in the game at launch! 

[b][h3]What is being worked on right now?[/h3][/b]Since the Steam page launch in December, I’ve focused on refining the Adventurer Registration Sequence. This serves as a test for implementing improved visuals and polishing features to completion.
Alongside this rework I’m working on connected systems such as : adventurer Progression and the balancing of it, the Faction Reputation System and adventurer and guild visualisation to make the whole experience feel more “alive”. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45322556/9f2a7c42418fe154d2976633dba9a0e19f3d006a.png[/img]
[i]A sneak peek at early prototyping to make the 'Adventurer Recruitment Sequence' feel more alive. Previously, candidate statuses were only reflected in the Adventurers' Ledger. Note that visuals, style, and layout are not final. [/i]

[b]That's it for this news! I Hope you are looking forward about what’s to come in 2025![/b]
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Remember to [b]Wishlist[/b] the game and stay connected with Adventurers Guild Inc. on your favourite platform! You can follow both the [url=https://bsky.app/profile/adv-guild-inc.bsky.social]game account[/url] and my [url=https://bsky.app/profile/trakaan-gamedev.bsky.social]gamedev account[/url] on Bluesky (where I’m most active), or check out the full Linktree [url=https://linktr.ee/vincentlgamedev][b]here[/b][/url] for all platforms.

notes.title: December Dev Update: What’s New in Adventurers Guild Inc.! 🛡️
notes.content:
[h2]Greetings, Guildmasters! 👋[/h2]

[b][h3]Thank You![/h3][/b]
First, I want to thank those of you that have already wishlisted the game! It makes a huge difference in terms of visibility, and you can’t even begin to imagine how good it feels to see more and more of you interested in this project.

[h3]What I’ve Been Working On[/h3]
[list]
[b][*] Progress Toward Playability (and a future playtest ?):[/b] No progress on the visual side this month, but the game is getting closer and closer to a playable state (which is the most important). The first playtesters will even get to try out some portions of the game during the holidays!

[b][*] Adventurer Admission Mechanic:[/b] I’m currently implementing the adventurer admission mechanic. It’s a crucial feature since it will determine what kind of adventurers are admitted into your guild and I want the flow for setting those elements to be as intuitive as possible so it's taking a bit more time than expected. I should be able to share more about this in the next update. 

[b][*] Update on what will be in the game at release:[/b] I’ve updated the game description, here on Steam, to reflect elements that I can confidently promise to be included when the game releases. That doesn’t mean I wasn't sure about those before or that those are the only mechanics in the game but simply that the current state of development now allows me to be more specific about these.
[/list]
for example here is a short breakdown of one of those :

[i][b]Turn-based Cyclical Gameplay :[/b]
This feature was so obvious to me that I forgot to put it in the description... This is now corrected and here is a quick breakdown:
[list]
[*]Each day is divided into 4 distinct phases: Night, Morning, Afternoon, and Evening. At the start of each phase, time stops, you review, plan, issue orders and finally press "play" to watch the guild come to life.
[*]Regular events like “Guild admission Saturday” or the monthly “Board Meeting” punctuate your game, giving you milestones to prepare for. 
[*] Dynamic events are tied to the world state and your previous choices. If you know what to look for, you can anticipate them and turn them to your advantage. If not, they'll surely mess up your carefully crafted plans!
[/list][/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45322556/264c35700b2711400920752686eb79d4c1855342.gif[/img]
[i]Here’s a look at the day-night cycle in action! (Note: The time-stopping mechanic isn’t shown here.)[/i]

[h2]What's next?[/h2]
In the next update, I’ll analyse feedback from the first playtesters and take a deep dive into adventurers: their admissions process, needs, and decision-making mechanics.

notes.title: Welcome to Adventurers Guild Inc.! 🏰✨
notes.content:
[h1]Hello, Guild Masters![/h1]

I’m incredibly excited to officially announce Adventurers Guild Inc. on Steam! 

The game is still in a [b]very early development stage[/b], but I couldn’t resist sharing a glimpse of what’s already in the works with this [b]Early Preview Trailer[/b]: 

[previewyoutube=FB5kb152WTo;full][/previewyoutube]

Where do quests  and the money to pay them come from? That’s the question that started it all! So, as a long-time fan of management and tycoon games, I decided it was time to give you, the players, the means to answer that question yourselves! 

[h2]What will you do in Adventurers Guild Inc.? 🎯[/h2]
    • [b]Build your Guild from the ground up[/b]: Place rooms, maintain them, and upgrade them to create a stress and injury free environment for your staff and adventurers (at least in theory!).
    • [b]Welcome, test, nurture, and profit from adventurers:[/b] Each adventurer comes with unique stats, quirks, and traits, and managing their needs is an adventure in itself!
    •[b] Balance chaos with strategy: [/b]Managing your guild’s budget, reputation, and the constant stream of client requests is no easy task!
    • [b]Choose how to leave your mark:[/b] Whether you thrive on quest posting, adventurer healing fees, or selling loot back to the merchant guild, the choice is yours in this low-tech, fantastical world brimming with humor.

[h2]How can you support this journey? 🌱[/h2]
Simple : Add Adventurers Guild Inc. to your [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/3297040/Adventurers_Guild_Inc/]Wishlist! [/url]
Wishlists are critical for visibility on Steam, and every single one helps reach a greater audience. It also allows me to realistically plan the scale of future improvements, including visuals, animations, music, voice acting, localization, and more. 
You can also help by:
    • Following this Steam page and the game’s [url=https://bsky.app/profile/adv-guild-inc.bsky.social]Bluesky[/url] and [url=https://x.com/Adv_Guild_Inc]Twitter (X[/url]) accounts for regular updates.
    • Sharing the game on your favorite social media platforms.
    • Following my game dev [url=https://bsky.app/profile/trakaan-gamedev.bsky.social]Bluesky[/url] account (if you’re interested in sneak peeks and dev rants).
    • Joining our [url=https://discord.gg/betxskbmCa]Discord[/url] to chat about the game, give feedback, and maybe even join future playtests!

[h2]What’s next ? 🔮[/h2]
I’ll be posting regular updates here on Steam, at least once a month (and hopefully every week or two if time allows). These updates will include sneak peeks, dev insights, and announcements about playtests and upcoming features.
On the development side, I’ll be:
    • Adding missing mechanics and polishing gameplay.
    • Enhancing visuals and animations.
    • Working on the Guild View: a big feature that’s currently too raw to show but will give you a closer look at the bustling life inside your guild. I hope to share progress on this real soon!
For now, enjoy this early glimpse of the QuestBoard Publishing System:

[h3]Thank You! [/h3]
[b]Thank you[/b] for taking the time to check out Adventurers Guild Inc.. This project has been a labor of love, and I’m so excited to see where this journey takes us together. 

This game is already a reality but [b]every wishlist, every comment, and every share helps bring it closer to its full potential![/b]

See you at the guild,
[i]Vincent L. 🛡️ (Head Guildmaster at the Adventurers Guild HQ)[/i]

https://store.steampowered.com/app/3297040/Adventurers_Guild_Inc/
